3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The privatization process had begun. And as I had expected, Sordland's two most prominent oligarchs wanted to speak to me about it.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The two men sat across the table from me, leaving an empty chair in between them.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Lucian showed Marcel Koronti and Walter Tusk into the conference room.

10.speaker: Marcel Koronti
10.text: “Old man. You always think so small.”

12.speaker: Walter Tusk
12.text: “Haven't you heard a word of what I said?”

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: The two men packed their belongings and left the meeting room.

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: He brought out a bottle of Erlory Maroon 30-year old.

19.speaker: Walter Tusk
19.text: “I heard Petr say that you favour this one.”

24.speaker: Marcel Koronti
24.text: “I will take my leave as well.”

25.speaker: Marcel Koronti
25.text: “I can do so much more to sway the public in your favour.”

27.speaker: Walter Tusk
27.text: “Hah. Nothing. It's just a token of friendship.”

28.speaker: Marcel Koronti
28.text: “Power over the Assembly is nothing compared to power over the people!”

31.speaker: Marcel Koronti
31.text: “I can give you power over both the Assembly and the Sordish public."

33.speaker: Walter Tusk
33.text: “I think we all have very busy schedules.”

34.speaker: Marcel Koronti
34.text: “Don't forget that I have something that gives me an edge over this man and his archaic ways. A powerful tool.”

35.speaker: Narrator
35.text: After the papers were signed, Marcel and Walter stood up.

36.speaker: Marcel Koronti
36.text: “These shares will increase my already considerable influence over newspapers, radio and television.”

37.speaker: Marcel Koronti
37.text: “You lack the vision to see the bigger picture."

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: Marcel approached me and we shook hands.

40.speaker: Walter Tusk
40.text: “Good. I hope you come to the right conclusion then.”

41.speaker: Marcel Koronti
41.text: “It's nice to see you, Mr. President.”

42.speaker: Lucian Galade
42.text: “You will need to sign here, here and here.”

44.speaker: Narrator
44.text: He took a set of car keys from his pocket and gave them to me.

45.speaker: Lucian Galade
45.text: “You will need to sign here, here and here.”

47.speaker: Lucian Galade
47.text: “You will need to sign here, here and here.”

48.speaker: Marcel Koronti
48.text: “But that is not all, Mr. President.”

50.speaker: Marcel Koronti
50.text: “Public opinion means everything when it comes to elections. And guess what?”

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: I looked out the window. On the road leading to the palace, I saw a glittering, brand-new Randorfini sports car. A car that only the richest of the richest in Sordland could afford.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: He pointed to various sections and pages in the stack of papers.

55.speaker: Player
55.text: “I can't accept a luxury car while the people of Sordland go hungry.”

56.speaker: Player
56.text: “Thank you, Marcel. I can't wait to drive it."

58.speaker: Marcel Koronti
58.text: “Of course you can. It's a gift.”

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: He pointed to various sections and pages in the stack of papers.

60.speaker: Narrator
60.text: He pointed to various sections and pages in the stack of papers.

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “Why are you two showering me with gifts?”

67.speaker: Marcel Koronti
67.text: “Which means I will have the same influence he does over the Assembly. I can sway them as you like.”

68.speaker: Narrator
68.text: Lucian put a stack of papers in front of Walter.

69.speaker: Narrator
69.text: Lucian put a stack of papers in front of Marcel and Walter.

70.speaker: Marcel Koronti
70.text: “Surely better than a bottle of whiskey.”

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: Lucian put a stack of papers in front of Marcel.

72.speaker: Lucian Galade
72.text: “So, Mr. Tusk and Mr. Koronti. President Rayne is about to sell private shares in Sordland's two largest national corporations. And now you're here, showering him with gifts."

74.speaker: Walter Tusk
74.text: “Do you think I can't do better?”

76.speaker: Marcel Koronti
76.text: “Don't forget that I have something that gives me an edge over this man and his archaic ways. A powerful tool.”

82.speaker: Marcel Koronti
82.text: “If you give me the shares, I will topple this old man.”

83.speaker: Player
83.text: “Thank you both. Let's begin the meeting.”

84.speaker: Marcel Koronti
84.text: “He could never *ever* hope to beat this offer.”

86.speaker: Marcel Koronti
86.text: “He can never *ever* hope to beat this offer.”

87.speaker: Marcel Koronti
87.text: “This is absolutely no bribe, Mr. President.”

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: They sat down. Lucian produced a set of documents from his briefcase. He put on his reading glasses.

93.speaker: Walter Tusk
93.text: “He can't do anything. He is not capable enough to--”

95.speaker: Marcel Koronti
95.text: “I want to be straightforward with you.”

98.speaker: Lucian Galade
98.text: “I bet this has nothing to do with the recent privatizations.”

99.speaker: Marcel Koronti
99.text: “Thank you for the wise decision, Mr. President. I will arrange a small transfer as a personal thanks.”

101.speaker: Lucian Galade
101.text: “Media is a powerful tool after all.”

102.speaker: Marcel Koronti
102.text: “But what he is sitting on top of right now was built by my father, Konrath Koronti.”

104.speaker: Walter Tusk
104.text: “Thank you for the wise decision, President. I'll send a token of my appreciation to your account.”

108.speaker: Marcel Koronti
108.text: “True, he might have command over some people in the Assembly.”

118.speaker: Walter Tusk
118.text: “Although I would've preferred you pick me, I respect that.”

119.speaker: Lucian Galade
119.text: “So, Mr. Tusk and Mr. Koronti. President Rayne is about to sell private shares in Nedam Mining Group. And now you're here, showering him with gifts."

121.speaker: Lucian Galade
121.text: “So, Mr. Tusk and Mr. Koronti. President Rayne is about to sell private shares in the Sordish State Corporation. And now you're here, showering him with gifts."

123.speaker: Lucian Galade
123.text: “You're both clearly more skilled at business than you are at subterfuge."

124.speaker: Marcel Koronti
124.text: “Haven't you heard a word of what I said?”

125.speaker: Walter Tusk
125.text: “You are twenty years early to be the head of the Lotherberg Group.”

126.speaker: Marcel Koronti
126.text: “Before you spew those big words, make sure you can actually do it, Walter.”

127.speaker: Lucian Galade
127.text: “So tell us: Why do you deserve to claim these shares before they go on the general market?"

130.speaker: Marcel Koronti
130.text: “Mr. President. First off, Mr. Tusk here is lying about the extent his influence.”

136.speaker: Walter Tusk
136.text: “That's why I want to help you.”

137.speaker: Walter Tusk
137.text: “Don't make light of me, President. I am saying this precisely because I believe you are capable of doing it.”

138.speaker: Player
138.text: “If I win, I will win with my own strength.”

139.speaker: Walter Tusk
139.text: “We, you and I, have been getting along like gangbusters recently.”

141.speaker: Walter Tusk
141.text: “We, you and I, haven't been on the best of terms lately.”

142.speaker: Walter Tusk
142.text: “I see. So you decided to not pick a side.”

145.speaker: Walter Tusk
145.text: “I want to continue this profitable relationship between us.”

146.speaker: Walter Tusk
146.text: “But I want to nurture a profitable relationship between us where we both win.”

147.speaker: Walter Tusk
147.text: “These shares are very important to me. If I had them, I could do so much more for Sordland."

148.speaker: Walter Tusk
148.text: “*I* made The Group what it is.”

149.speaker: Player
149.text: “The shares will be equally distributed between the two of you. [Insider Trading]"

150.speaker: Player
150.text: “The shares will go to Marcel. [Insider Trading +1 Personal Wealth]"

152.speaker: Walter Tusk
152.text: “You haven't even seen what I and my connections are capable of."

153.speaker: Player
153.text: “The shares will go to Walter. [Insider Trading +1 Personal Wealth]"

154.speaker: Walter Tusk
154.text: “Do you want to get re-elected? No problem. I will make sure of it.”

156.speaker: Walter Tusk
156.text: “This is my offer to you. I will do whatever it takes to make you President for another term.”

160.speaker: Player
160.text: “No matter how you bribe me, you won't get what you are here for.”

162.speaker: Player
162.text: "I'm sick of these shenanigans. You'll have to squabble over the shares when they enter the market, just like everyone else."

163.speaker: Marcel Koronti
163.text: “Haven't you heard a word of what I said?”

165.speaker: Walter Tusk
165.text: “Yeah. Can't you see how good of a deal I'm offering here?"

166.speaker: Lucian Galade
166.text: “I believe the President has already told you his decision, Mr. Tusk, Mr. Koronti.”

167.speaker: Lucian Galade
167.text: “We are terribly busy today, so I would like to wish you a good day as well.”

168.speaker: Lucian Galade
168.text: “I hope you know where the door is. If you don't, you can ask a security guard to show you out.”

187.speaker: Player
187.text: "Nope. You said the car was a gift."

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: Marcel slowly shook his head at me. There were storm clouds gathering in his eyes.

190.speaker: Marcel Koronti
190.text: "Your days of being adored by the media are over, Rayne. And so is your presidency."

201.speaker: Walter Tusk
201.text: "Nice try, brat. But you're not half the man your father was."

205.speaker: Walter Tusk
205.text: "Thanks for the shares, President. As the current and future leader of the Lotherberg Group, I shall not let you down."

207.speaker: Walter Tusk
207.text: "Enjoy the whiskey, President. While you can."

211.speaker: Narrator
211.text: Lucian handed him the paperwork. He made a big show of signing it.

212.speaker: Narrator
212.text: Lucian handed him the paperwork. He made a big show of signing it, then passed it on to Marcel, who begrudgingly signed as well.

221.speaker: Player
221.text: “The shares will go to Marcel. [Insider Trading]"

222.speaker: Player
222.text: “The shares will go to Walter. [Insider Trading]"
